top_choice_rationale: P001 credits Katori and Ye for the magic-wavelength optical lattice clock, a new regime in which light shifts cancel while many atoms are interrogated, reaching 1e-18 performance that independent laboratories have reproduced and compared. The two-name allocation is clean and the citation can isolate the lattice concept from the 2005 and 2012 metrology prizes. P002 is a real invention that overcame a long-standing limit, but it is an enabling instrument, the STEM corrector work is left uncredited, and only one member supports it. I still prefer it to no award.
recusal_note: I direct WACQT and work on superconducting circuits at Chalmers, so I would recuse on B001 (circuit QED), which is not on this slate. I am a Chalmers colleague of Eva Olsson, who supports P002, though I do not work in electron microscopy. I have no tie to the P001 laureates.
